questionText: Modern technology can not replace human interactions. Do you agree? Refer to the text in support of your answer. (50 words in total)

rows.verbatim: The answers the scheme accepts in full
rows.contextNote: The examination prints this question in English and it is answered in English or in Irish, not in Lithuanian. The scheme awards half marks for an answer given in the wrong language.

options: Candidates may choose to agree or disagree using the following points.
Even with modern technologies, a part of tasks must be done by people.
Customers expect at least some sort of human interaction during transactions.
Modern technologies do only what they are asked for. Humans are more inteligent and adaptive.
Even with modern technologies people do not love their humanity and human interaction is still important to them.
Modern technologies are meant to make people‘s live easier but should not completely replace humans.
If something brakes, people will fix it. So interaction between the modern technologies and the humans is both ways: one serve / help another.
Modern technologies can create a gap between the new and old people‘s generations.
This can lead to some services being provided through machines only. Which can exclude some potential customers as they would not know how to use the technologies.
Modern technologies could make people be less motivated to interact with other people.
Modern technologies can indeed replace the human interation with Artificial

Modern technologies could be more efficient without a risk of loosing a motivation. This could be a risk to humans who might be less efficient, however, machines cannot fulfil the need of an actual human interaction.

notes: The scheme prints the tariff as '6 marks'; the paper prints this ask on page 9 of the question booklet. Paper/scheme wording agreement 0.94.
